topic: What interference mitigation techniques are viable for overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations?
consensus_response: Holographic MIMO (H-MIMO) and Non-Coherent Detection (NCD) can effectively mitigate interference in satellite-terrestrial systems. H-MIMO's spatial selectivity creates precise beams that reduce overlap, while NCD leverages non-coherent detection to handle noise and multipath fading. Machine Learning-based Signal Processing (MLSP) can enhance the performance of these techniques by adaptively adjusting signal processing parameters based on real-time channel conditions. This combination balances performance and resource utilization, ensuring robust communication even under challenging conditions.
reference_context: Interference mitigation techniques for overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations include Rate Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA), Time Division Multiple Access (TDMA), Hybrid Automatic Repeat Request (HARQ), and Machine Learning-based Signal Processing (MLSP). These techniques aim to reduce co-channel interference, improve spectral efficiency, and maintain high integrity transmission in safety-critical aeronautical applications.
